nodes.name: Joinings and disjointness
nodes.statement: Let X and Y be Gamma-flows. We view X times Y as a Gamma-flow with the diagonal action of Gamma. A emphdjoining of X and Y is a subflow Z subseteq X times Y that projects onto X and Y. The Gamma-flows X, Y are emphddisjoint, in symbols X perp Y, if their only joining is X times Y itself.

The $\Gamma$-flows $X$, $Y$ are \emphd{disjoint}, in symbols $X \perp Y$, if their only joining is $X \times Y$ itself.

\label{defn:sep}
        Let $s \in \mathbb{N}^+$ and let $\Phi \subset \Gamma$ be a finite subset. An \emphd{$(s,\Phi)$-separator} is a mapping $x \colon \Gamma \to (s+1)$ such that 
        for all $0 \leqslant i \leqslant s$, the set $x^{-1}(s) \subseteq \Gamma$ is
        $\Phi$-finite \ep{with respect to the left multiplication action $\Gamma \mathrel{\reflectbox{$\righttoleftarrow$}} \Gamma$}. The set of all $(s,\Phi)$-separators is denoted by $\mathsf{Sep}(s,\Phi)$.

nodes.name: Asymptotic separators
nodes.statement: For the remainder of the paper, we fix an enumeration (Phi_n)_n in N of the finite subsets of Gamma in which every set appears infinitely often. Given s in N^+, we let \[ Sep(s) \,coloneqq\, prod_n in N Sep(s, Phi_n). \] The space Sep(s) is equipped with the product topology and the diagonal action of Gamma. We call the elements of Sep(s) emphdasymptotic s-separators.

To this end, we introduce a family of ``bad'' random events analogous to the one in the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:SFT}. Let $k = \set{0,\ldots, k-1}$ carry the uniform probability measure and consider the 
        space $k^X$ with the product measure $\mathbb{P}$. For each $x \in X$, let 
        \[
            B_x \,\coloneqq\, \big\{f \in k^X \,:\, \text{the map $W \to k \colon \sigma \mapsto f(\sigma \cdot x)$ is not in $\mathcal{P}$}\big\},
        \]

        \[

nodes.statement: Let (X_n)_n in N be a countable family of Polish Gamma-flows with no wandering points. We seek a free minimal subflow of 2^Gamma that is disjoint from every X_n. For each n in N, we fix a countable basis (U_n,m)_m in N for the topology on X_n consisting of nonempty open sets. Lemma~ implies that each family F(U_n,m) is unbounded. By Corollary~, there is a free subflow Y subset 2^Gamma that is F(U_n,m)-minimal for all n, m in N; in particular, Y is minimal. Note that if U subseteq X_n is a nonempty open set, then Y is F(U)-minimal because F(U) supseteq F(U_n,m) for any basic open set U_n,m subseteq U. Therefore, Proposition~ implies that X_n perp Y for all n in N, as desired.
